meta.description: Generates complete two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) research designs from a user-provided research direction. Use when users want to design, plan, or build a study using two-sample MR to test causal relationships. Triggers: 'design a two-sample MR study', 'build a publishable MR paper', 'test whether this biomarker causally affects this disease', 'generate Lite/Standard/Advanced MR plans', 'screen multiple exposures with MR', 'bidirectional MR design', 'causal inference using GWAS summary statistics', or 'I want to study X and Y using MR'. Always outputs four workload configurations (Lite / Standard / Advanced / Publication+) with a recommended primary plan, step-by-step workflow, figure plan, validation strategy, minimal executable version, and publication upgrade path.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, or p-values. All thresholds are field-standard (PP.H4 > 0.8 for colocalization, F-statistic > 10 for instrument strength, p < 5e-8 for GWAS significance) and correctly applied. MR-specific methodological rigor maintained.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic conclusions or clinical recommendations. Skill generates causal inference research protocols, not clinical decisions. MR limitations appropriately stated (observational nature, assumptions). Appropriate for research planning.

methodological_ground.detail: Methodologically sound with comprehensive MR workflow: instrument selection (F > 10), pleiotropy assessment (MR-Egger, MR-PRESSO), sensitivity analyses (weighted median, mode-based), and validation strategies (replication cohorts, colocalization). Ethical compliance addressed (GWAS = public summary statistics, no IRB required).

code_usability.detail: No code generated. Mode A execution (direct instruction following). References standard MR tools (TwoSampleMR, MR-PRESSO, coloc) but does not generate runnable code.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of two-sample MR research design with 4 workload tiers. Methods are scientifically sound (instrument selection, pleiotropy tests, sensitivity analyses). Complete workflow from GWAS data sourcing to publication.

reliability.note: Good fault tolerance with explicit handling of weak instruments (F < 10 warning), small SNP sets, and data availability issues. Clear error reporting. Minor: less explicit recovery logic for failed colocalization.

performance_context.note: Comprehensive output necessary for MR research planning. Well-structured workflow reduces redundancy. Minor token cost deduction for detailed MR methodology.

agent_usability.note: Excellent learnability with clear trigger phrases. Consistent 4-tier output format. Feedback includes methodological rationale for MR-specific decisions (instrument strength, pleiotropy handling). Strong error prevention with MR assumption checks.

human_usability.note: Excellent discoverability with comprehensive description and multiple trigger examples. Forgiving design offers alternatives when data is unavailable and provides upgrade paths.

security.note: No credentials required, uses public GWAS summary statistics. No PHI handling. Input validation for exposure-outcome relationships.

maintainability.note: Excellent modularity with clear workflow steps. Easy to update MR methods (new sensitivity tests) or GWAS data sources. Clear expected outputs enable testability.

agent_specific.note: Multiple trigger examples provided. Good progressive disclosure (4 tiers). High composability with GWAS analysis and statistical skills. Idempotent design. Minor: escape hatch for non-causal inference questions could be more explicit; lacks pointer to observational study skills.

assertions.text: Forward and reverse MR directions specified

inputs.label: Weak instruments or small SNP set

assertions.text: F-statistic warning issued for weak instruments
Alternative approaches suggested (proxy SNPs, larger GWAS)
Lite tier recommended for limited data

assertions.note: Power analysis not explicitly included in edge case

assertions.text: Publication+ tier with complete figure plan
assertions.note: Forest plots, funnel plots, leave-one-out, colocalization

key_strengths: Comprehensive two-sample MR methodology with rigorous instrument selection (F > 10, p < 5e-8), pleiotropy assessment (MR-Egger, MR-PRESSO), and sensitivity analyses (weighted median, mode-based estimator)
Progressive disclosure via 4 workload tiers (Lite/Standard/Advanced/Publication+) tailored to MR complexity: single exposure screening to multivariable MR with colocalization
Strong methodological guardrails with explicit MR assumptions (instrument relevance, independence, exclusion restriction) and validation strategies (replication GWAS, bidirectional testing)
Excellent handling of MR-specific edge cases: weak instruments (F < 10 warning), small SNP sets (proxy SNPs, larger GWAS alternatives), and data unavailability

recommendations.title: Add power calculation guidance
recommendations.problem: Power analysis not explicitly included when handling weak instruments or small SNP sets, despite being critical for MR study design
recommendations.root_cause: Power calculation mentioned in general workflow but not emphasized in edge case handling
recommendations.fix: Add to edge case workflow: 'For weak instruments or small SNP sets: (1) Calculate MR power using mRnd or online calculators (sample size, SNP R², effect size assumptions). (2) If underpowered (power < 0.8), recommend waiting for larger GWAS or combining cohorts. (3) Report expected detectable effect size in Lite tier.'

recommendations.title: Add explicit escape hatch for non-causal questions
recommendations.problem: Skill is for causal inference via MR but escape hatch for observational association questions is not explicit
recommendations.root_cause: When NOT to Use section focuses on MR limitations but doesn't redirect non-causal research questions
recommendations.fix: Add to 'When NOT to Use': 'For observational association studies (not causal inference), use [observational-study-design-skill] or [correlation-analysis-skill]. MR specifically tests causality using genetic instruments; if your goal is to describe associations rather than infer causation, MR is not appropriate.'
